description: Daily Quiz sets shown on /quiz, keyed by date (YYYY-MM-DD, India time). Each set has 5 MCQs. New sets are added only after Kenil approves them in chat. The first set below is a sample drawn from existing module quiz items.

questions.stem: A patient with DKA has K⁺ 3.0 mmol/L and is about to start insulin. There is no other emergency. What's the best next step?
options: Start insulin now and replace potassium later
Hold insulin and replace potassium first, until K⁺ is at least 3.3 mmol/L
Give 50 mL of 8.4% sodium bicarbonate, then start insulin
Give a 50% dextrose bolus, then start insulin
questions.explanation: Starting insulin when K⁺ is below 3.3 mmol/L can cause dangerous hypokalaemia. Replace potassium first, then start insulin.

reference.label: Umpierrez GE, et al. Hyperglycemic crises in adults with diabetes: a consensus report. Diabetes Care 2024

questions.stem: A man's baseline creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL. After a day in ICU it is 2.2 mg/dL, and urine output has been 0.4 mL/kg/h for 14 hours. What is the KDIGO AKI stage?
questions.explanation: KDIGO stage 2 is a 2.0–2.9-fold rise in creatinine or urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/h for 12 hours or more. Stage 3 needs a 3-fold rise, creatinine ≥ 4.0 mg/dL, RRT, or more severe oliguria.

reference.label: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury. Kidney Int Suppl 2012

questions.stem: A woman with septic shock has been resuscitated. She is not bleeding and has no acute coronary syndrome. Her Hb is 7.4 g/dL. Best transfusion plan?
options: Transfuse to a target of 9–10 g/dL
Hold blood; transfuse at Hb < 7, target 7–9
Give 2 units now because she is on noradrenaline
questions.explanation: TRISS and SSC support a restrictive threshold of 7 g/dL in septic shock without active bleeding or acute coronary syndrome.

reference.label: Holst LB, et al. Lower versus higher hemoglobin threshold for transfusion in septic shock (TRISS). N Engl J Med 2014; SSC 2026

questions.stem: A comatose adult has ROSC after cardiac arrest. There is no separate indication for hypothermia to 33°C. What should you do about temperature?
options: Allow fever up to 39°C if the patient is otherwise stable
Prevent fever, keeping temperature at 37.5°C or below
Warm to 38.5°C to improve neurological recovery
questions.explanation: TTM2 and current ILCOR, ERC and AHA guidance favour preventing fever over routine cooling to 33°C after ROSC.

reference.label: Dankiewicz J, et al. Hypothermia versus normothermia after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (TTM2). N Engl J Med 2021

questions.stem: A patient develops anaphylaxis (wheeze, low BP, urticaria) after a drug. What is the first-line treatment?
options: IV adrenaline 1 mg, as in cardiac arrest
IM adrenaline 0.5 mg (1:1000) into the anterolateral mid-thigh
IV hydrocortisone 200 mg as the first drug
Subcutaneous adrenaline 0.3 mg into the arm
questions.explanation: First-line treatment is IM adrenaline 0.5 mg of 1:1000 in the anterolateral mid-thigh. IV adrenaline is reserved for peri-arrest or a titrated infusion by experienced staff. Steroids are only adjuncts.

reference.label: Resuscitation Council UK. Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis: guidelines 2021

questions.stem: A patient with a confirmed PE has BP 80/50 that has stayed low for 20 minutes and a dilated RV on echo. There's no contraindication to bleeding. What's the best next step?
questions.explanation: High-risk (haemodynamically unstable) PE needs reperfusion, and systemic thrombolysis is first-line.

reference.label: ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism. Eur Heart J 2019

questions.stem: A man with Guillain-Barré syndrome has worsening weakness. Which finding most strongly points to elective intubation?
questions.explanation: The "20/30/40" rule is FVC below 20 mL/kg, MIP weaker than −30 cmH₂O and MEP below 40 cmH₂O. SpO₂ and PaCO₂ worsen late.

reference.label: Lawn ND, et al. Anticipating mechanical ventilation in Guillain-Barré syndrome. Arch Neurol 2001

questions.stem: A woman took paracetamol tablets repeatedly over about 12 hours (a staggered overdose). She feels well, and her ALT is normal. What's the right approach?
options: Plot the level on the nomogram and treat only if it's above the line
Start IV acetylcysteine without waiting for the level
Repeat the level in 4 hours, then decide
questions.explanation: The nomogram can't be read after a staggered overdose or when the time is unknown, so start acetylcysteine.

reference.label: MHRA Drug Safety Update. Treating paracetamol overdose with intravenous acetylcysteine: new guidance. 2012

questions.stem: A trauma patient arrives 1 hour after injury with bleeding and haemorrhagic shock. What does the evidence say about tranexamic acid?
options: Give 1 g IV over 10 minutes within 3 hours, then 1 g over 8 hours
Avoid it because of clot risk
Give it only if fibrinogen is low
questions.explanation: CRASH-2 showed lower mortality when TXA was given early. Starting it after 3 hours didn't help and may cause harm.

reference.label: CRASH-2 trial collaborators. Effects of tranexamic acid on death, vascular occlusive events, and transfusion in trauma patients. Lancet 2010

questions.stem: On day 7 of UFH, a patient's platelets fall from 250 to 95 ×10⁹/L and a new DVT appears. The 4Ts score is high. What's the best step?
options: Stop all heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant (e.g. argatroban or fondaparinux)
Stop heparin and give no anticoagulant
questions.explanation: Suspected HIT with thrombosis needs every form of heparin stopped, LMWH included, and a non-heparin anticoagulant started. Platelets are avoided.

reference.label: Cuker A, et al. American Society of Hematology 2018 guidelines for HIT. Blood Adv 2018

questions.stem: A woman at 34 weeks has an eclamptic seizure. Best first drug?
options: Magnesium sulphate 4 g IV over 15-20 min
questions.explanation: Magnesium is first-line for eclampsia (4 g IV load, then 1 g/h for 24 h) and beats diazepam and phenytoin at preventing further seizures.

reference.label: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia. Obstet Gynecol 2020; Magpie Trial, Lancet 2002

questions.stem: Chronic hyponatraemia, Na+ 112, in a malnourished man with alcohol use disorder and no severe symptoms. Maximum safe rise in Na+ in the first 24 h?
questions.explanation: High osmotic-demyelination risk (alcohol, malnutrition, hypokalaemia): aim for 4-8 and never exceed 8 mmol/L in 24 h; the limit is 10 for others.

reference.label: Verbalis JG et al. Diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of hyponatremia: expert panel recommendations. Am J Med 2013

questions.stem: Seizures continue after two adequate doses of lorazepam. Correct next step?
questions.explanation: Second-line drugs must be given at full loading dose. In ESETT, levetiracetam 60 mg/kg, valproate 40 mg/kg and fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg each stopped seizures in about half of patients.

reference.label: Kapur J et al. Randomized trial of three anticonvulsant medications for status epilepticus (ESETT). N Engl J Med 2019

questions.stem: Cirrhosis with a variceal bleed, stable after resuscitation (Hb 7.8 g/dL, HR 102, BP 108/70). Best transfusion plan?
options: Hold blood; transfuse at Hb ≤ 7, target 7-8
questions.explanation: Restrictive transfusion: over-transfusion raises portal pressure and rebleeding. FFP isn't used to correct INR in cirrhosis.

reference.label: de Franchis R et al. Baveno VII: Renewing consensus in portal hypertension. J Hepatol 2022

questions.stem: A ventilated patient is CAM-ICU positive but calm and not distressed. Best approach?
options: Find and treat causes, ABCDEF bundle, re-screen every shift
questions.explanation: Haloperidol and ziprasidone did not shorten delirium (MIND-USA) and PADIS 2025 does not recommend routine antipsychotics; benzodiazepines and restraints worsen it.

reference.label: PADIS 2025 guideline update. Crit Care Med 2025; Girard TD et al. MIND-USA, N Engl J Med 2018

questions.stem: A 45-year-old with septic shock from aspiration pneumonia also has a traumatic brain injury from a fall. Which resuscitation fluid does SSC 2026 suggest?
questions.explanation: SSC 2026 suggests balanced crystalloids over saline in sepsis, but with a remark to use 0.9% saline when sepsis coexists with traumatic brain injury; starches are recommended against.

reference.label: Prescott HC, et al. Executive summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026. Crit Care Med. 2026 (statement 44 and remark)

questions.stem: A farmer with fever, an eschar, hypotension and PaO2/FiO2 of 180 is diagnosed with severe scrub typhus. Best antimicrobial regimen?
options: IV doxycycline plus IV azithromycin for 7 days
questions.explanation: In INTREST, combination IV doxycycline plus azithromycin reduced the composite of death, persistent complications or fever at day 7 compared with either drug alone; beta-lactams have no activity against Orientia.

reference.label: Varghese GM, et al. Intravenous doxycycline, azithromycin, or both for severe scrub typhus (INTREST). N Engl J Med. 2023;388(9):792-803

questions.stem: You perform a 20-minute whole blood clotting test (20WBCT) after a suspected viper bite. Which detail is essential for a valid result?
options: Use a new, clean, dry glass tube left undisturbed for 20 minutes
Use a plastic tube kept on ice
questions.explanation: Glass activates clotting; plastic, washed or wet tubes and disturbing the sample give false results. Blood that is still liquid when tilted at 20 minutes means venom-induced coagulopathy and is an indication for ASV.

reference.label: Lamb T, et al. The 20-minute whole blood clotting test (20WBCT) for snakebite coagulopathy: systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2021;15(8):e0009657

questions.stem: A ventilated ARDS patient has PaO2/FiO2 of 110 on FiO2 0.7 and PEEP 12 despite lung-protective ventilation for 12 hours. Next best step?
options: Increase tidal volume to 8-10 mL/kg PBW
Prone positioning for at least 16 hours per session
Inhaled nitric oxide as a mortality-reducing therapy
questions.explanation: PROSEVA showed lower mortality with early prone positioning (≥16 h sessions) when P/F is below 150 mmHg on FiO2 ≥0.6 and PEEP ≥5; HFOV and iNO have not improved survival.

reference.label: Guérin C, et al. Prone positioning in severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSEVA). N Engl J Med. 2013;368(23):2159-2168

questions.stem: In septic shock with lactic acidosis, which patient fits the Surviving Sepsis Campaign suggestion to give IV sodium bicarbonate?
options: Any patient with lactate above 4 mmol/L, to improve vasopressor response
questions.explanation: SSC suggests against bicarbonate for hypoperfusion-related lactic acidaemia, except in severe acidaemia (pH ≤7.2) with AKI stage 2-3. A Nov 2026 meta-analysis found fewer patients needed RRT with bicarbonate but no clear survival benefit.

reference.label: Prescott HC, Antonelli M, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Med. 2026;52(5):863-936

sets.title: Starter set: drawn from the module quizzes

questions.stem: Which hour-1 bundle element carries a STRONG recommendation in SSC 2026?
options: Antibiotics within 1 h in septic shock
questions.explanation: Antibiotics immediately (ideally within 1 h) in septic shock or probable sepsis is strong; 'at least 30 mL/kg' remains conditional with low-certainty evidence, and SSC 2026 suggests crystalloid alone over added albumin.

reference.label: Prescott HC, Antonelli M, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Med. 2026;52(5):863-936. Co-published in Crit Care Med. 2026 (doi:10.1097/CCM.0000000000007075)
